sources.entry: DockLens - Hover a Dock icon to see live thumbnails of all that app's windows, then switch, close or minimize them. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/firstfu/DockLens-app)

summary.one_liner: DockLens is a free, open-source macOS app that shows live thumbnails of an app's windows when you hover its Dock icon, letting you switch, close, minimize or full-screen them from the preview.
keywords: jump to window on other desktop
summary.what_it_does: DockLens detects which Dock icon the pointer is over (using the Accessibility permission) and shows a preview of that app's open windows. With Screen Recording allowed, the previews are live thumbnails captured locally; without it, the preview lists windows by app icon and title. From the preview you can click to switch to a window, close, minimize/restore or full-screen it, and use header buttons for new window, hide app or quit app. Minimized windows and windows on other Spaces are also listed, and windows closed in apps that keep running (such as Notion or Slack) stay listed so one click reopens them. It also offers a read-only Calendar agenda with a Join button, a Spotify and Music playback bar, and a Recently closed list of files in file-based apps that can be reopened. Single-key shortcuts (W, M, H, Q) work while the pointer is on the preview and can be turned off.
use_cases: switch between windows of an app from the Dock
close or minimize a window without opening it
find a window hidden on another desktop or minimized
reopen a document you just closed
see today's calendar events and join a meeting link
control Spotify or Music playback from the Dock
how_to_run: Or download DockLens.zip from Releases, unzip, and move DockLens.app to /Applications
Open the app, click Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security once, then grant the requested permissions
git clone the repository and cd DockLens-app
xcodebuild -project DockLens.xcodeproj -scheme DockLens -configuration Release -derivedDataPath build build
stack: macOS Accessibility, Screen Recording, Automation and Calendars APIs
notable: Live window thumbnails on Dock hover, with a fallback to icon-and-title list when Screen Recording is not granted
Lists closed-but-running windows (Notion, Slack) so they can be reopened with one click
Recently closed document list kept only in memory, never written to disk
Event-driven design claimed at 0% CPU when idle (measured on Apple silicon)
34 interface languages following the macOS language setting; universal binary for Apple silicon and Intel
caveats: Not notarized by Apple yet, so the first launch must be allowed manually in System Settings
Translations are AI-assisted and not all checked by native speakers
